findings.reason: The protected Python solution implements TwoSum by storing element frequencies in a hash map counts. add(number) increments counts[number] in O(1) expected time. find(value) iterates over distinct keys in counts, checking if complement = value - number exists, requiring count >= 2 when complement == number. The solution achieves O(1) add, O(u) find (u distinct elements), and O(u) auxiliary space; no candidate is required.
Tracking value frequencies in a hash map allows find to inspect complement presence and distinguish distinct elements (count >= 1) from self-pairs (count >= 2).
add takes O(1) time per number. find takes O(u) time where u is the number of distinct elements stored. Auxiliary space is O(u) for the frequency map. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts operations and argument lists, returning a list of bool or None responses for TwoSum initialization, add, and find calls.

The approach accurately details add vs find trade-off selection, hash map frequency representation, self-pair vs distinct-pair multiplicity checks, and O(1) add / O(u) find / O(u) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover precomputed pair sum quadratic add trade-offs, sorted array two-pointer insertion costs, plain set multiplicity failure modes, negative number and zero complement handling, and stream workload optimization choices.
